notes: §1985:VI.5.9.3 SR4: "The maximum number of characters allowed in the character-string is 30." AnalyzeCharacterString, the body every PictureAnalyzer.Analyze call runs, counts the characters of the character-string as written (spaces left out, a repetition factor counted as its own characters) and raises COBOL2146 when the count exceeds MaxStringLength(edition.DialectLevel); MaxStringLength returns MaxPictureStringLength85 (30) for an edition that has neither the picture-string-63-2014 nor the picture-string-50-2002 construct, which is how --std 85 reaches the 1985 bound. The check is an error, not an edition gate, so --permissive does not relax it. Probed at 85: 30 X accepted and 31 X refused; 9(1) seven times then 99 (30 characters) accepted and then 999 (31) refused; a 30-character numeric edited string accepted and its 31-character twin refused; 31 lowercase x refused. The witness is the 31 X refusal.

next.reason: 1985: 'The maximum number of characters allowed in the character-string is 30.' §2023:13.18.40.3 SR4: 'The maximum number of characters allowed in character-string-1 is 63', and §2023:13.18.40.3 SR6 counts a constant-name repetition factor by its integer's length. A character-string of 31 to 63 characters, refused in 1985, is accepted. Both are compile-time limits.
